near_miss.lead: vessel full of precious stuff: ON kistill ... fullur af silfri ~ Ved. somena pūrṇam kalaśam (*pl̥h1nós ~ pṛ-)
near_miss.why_not: Only the 'full' word is cognate; contents (silver vs soma) and context (hoard under a dead man's feet vs ritual vessel) differ; 'full of X' is generic. Greek partners empty.

near_miss.lead: measure in feet: ON sjö feta rúm ~ Gk ... πόδες
near_miss.why_not: Harald's 'seven feet of English ground' is a saga dictum, not inherited; Herodotus gives a tunnel's dimensions; foot-measures are generic.

near_miss.lead: wolf ~ man: ON Úlfs ~ ORu мужь ... аки волкъ
near_miss.why_not: ON Úlfr is the personal name of Úlfr stallari, not 'wolf'; no shared figure.

near_miss.lead: die with honour or win with victory: deyja hér með sóma eða vinna England með sigri
near_miss.why_not: Battle-speech choice of death or victory is universal rhetoric; Thucydides partner (naval disposition) shares nothing; no cognate collocation.

near_miss.lead: speak truly / fight for the realm (Tostig's message)
near_miss.why_not: Herodotus partner (Panionios selling eunuchs) unrelated; only everyday roots shared.

near_miss.lead: milking cows: ON mjólka kýr ~ OIr oc blegon bó / bó blicht (*h2melǵ- + *gʷōws)
near_miss.why_not: Exact cognate verb+object pair, but it is the literal name of a daily farm task; collocates_8c --pair shows it frequent in Celtic (24 of 122 *h2melǵ- units) and in Greek only in late prose (βοῦς ἀμέλγειν); no shared poetic or narrative context (Grettir: housewife goes to byre; TBC: Morrígan as hag milking). Generic, not phraseology.

near_miss.lead: bond: ON band (legal bond) ~ Ved. varuṇasya bandhaḥ
near_miss.why_not: Church-law 'band' vs Varuṇa's fetter; one shared root, different syntax and context.

near_miss.lead: in sleep: ON kveðin vísa í svefni fyr Haraldi ~ Gk εἶδε ὄψιν ἐν τῷ ὕπνῳ (*swep-/*sup-no-)
near_miss.why_not: 'In sleep' with the cognate noun is a generic dream-report frame (also Lat in somnis, Ved. svápne); the ON is a verse heard in sleep, not a vision seen; vísa is not cognate with ὄψις/εἶδε in this sense.

near_miss.lead: rib(s): ON þrjú rifin brotnuðu ~ ON undan hverju rifi koma köld ráð ~ byliny ребро
near_miss.why_not: Same branch for the two ON passages; the byliny hit is an editor's footnote, not epic text; broken ribs in a fight are not a formula.

near_miss.lead: verse as crafted object: fegri sé vísan ef grafin er
near_miss.why_not: Idea of polishing/engraving verse recalls IE poet-as-craftsman imagery, but no cognate wording in any partner (Russian гребу 'row' is a false root match); not claimable.

near_miss.lead: kin apposition: dóttur X ... systur Y ~ Ved. śraddhāyā duhitā ... svasā ṛṣīṇām
near_miss.why_not: Daughter/sister apposition is the natural way to identify a woman (collocates --pair: 79 Germanic, byliny, dainos, Armenian hits); Icelandic genealogical prose vs a hymn to the girdle; generic.

near_miss.lead: kin apposition: Gyðu dóttur Þorgils ... systur Úlfs jarls ~ Ved. duhitā ... svasā
near_miss.why_not: As BS-1c12b: generic identification of a woman by father and brother.

near_miss.lead: kin apposition: Rannveigu dóttur Ásmundar ... systur Grettis ~ asurāṇāṃ duhitā asi sā devānām asi svasā ~ ORu сестрѹ и ... доцерь
near_miss.why_not: Vedic 'daughter of A, sister of B' is attractive (cf. Uṣas divó duhitā ... svásā) but the ON is plain genealogy and the birchbark letter lists two women; apposition by kin terms is universal. Not claimed.
